text: Let R = {x | x ∉ x}, so that R ∈ R ⇔ R ∉ R. What does Russell's paradox establish about naive set theory?
choices: Some sets legitimately contain themselves as elements
Unrestricted comprehension — forming {x | P(x)} for every predicate P — is inconsistent
The collection of all sets is countable
Set membership fails to be a well-defined relation
explanation: The contradiction shows that not every predicate carves out a set: the naive comprehension axiom must be abandoned. Axiomatic set theory (ZFC) replaces it with separation, which only forms subsets of an already-given set.
